title: Model for Improvement
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The model, developed by Associates in Process Improvement, has three questions (aim, measures, changes) and uses Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles to test changes on a small scale before spreading them. No page date shown.

title: User security roles
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Article dated 30 Sep 2026. Six roles: Scheduler (bookings, basic patient details, SMS; no financials, treatment notes or completed forms), Receptionist (adds invoices and payments), Power receptionist (also deletes patients, archives invoices), Practitioner, Bookkeeper (exports financial data), Administrator (nearly everything; Cliniko advises not giving it to just anyone).

title: Virtual reception and Cliniko: a guide for practice owners
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 8 Mar 2024. Each outside receptionist needs their own login; shared logins are not safe for patient health data; sharing a two-factor code is not allowed; choose Scheduler, Receptionist or Power receptionist by need.

title: Staff Access Levels
supports: Opened with WebFetch. No page date beyond 2026 copyright. Levels from No Access to Account Owner; Front Desk collects payments, adds adjustments and writes off invoices; Access Billing and Access Charts switches; Account Owner authorises data exports or transfers.

title: Set up patient recalls
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 20 Sep 2024. Only Administrators and Power receptionists create recall types (1 to 100 days, weeks or months); most users apply recalls; Reports > Recalls with a Recalled tick; follow-up contact is manual.

title: How to create a new recall automation workflow
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 24 Aug 2026. Workflows by recall type with stages; each stage has an interval and a first and fallback template (SMS, email or letter); new workflows are inactive by default.

title: How to set a patient's recall preferences
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 24 Aug 2026. Separate dentist and hygienist recall intervals and the recall method are set in the Clinical section of the patient record; due dates update automatically unless edited.

title: Recall (Open Dental Manual v24.4)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Recall types set a default interval that can be changed per patient; completing a trigger procedure sets the next due date; status best updated on the Recall List; recalls can be disabled until a date or until a family balance drops below an amount. No page date.

title: Return Visit Reminders
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Staff set a suggested date and reminder date; Email (Auto) sends at 7am on the reminder date, only if no visit is booked; manual email and phone lists; automatic email on the Thrive plan. No page date.

title: Email and SMS Reminders
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reminders set in hours or days before; email on all plans; SMS only on Legacy, Practice or Thrive and in select regions; patients must consent before SMS; Do Not Text option. No page date.

title: Using Automatic Wait List Notifications
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Triggered by a cancellation, deletion or move; buffer of 15 minutes if the slot is within 24 hours, 2 hours if later; exclusive access period for notified clients; Thrive or Legacy plans only. No page date.

title: US Insurance Billing Training (category)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Steps from adding insurers and CPT rates, codes on visits, claim submission folders and EDI submission, rejections, posting insurer responses and EOBs, resubmissions, to the accounts receivable report.

title: Understanding costs in advance: good faith estimates
publisher: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Page modified 5 Oct 2026. Uninsured or self-pay patients get an estimate; booked 3 to 9 business days ahead: within 1 business day; 10 or more: within 3 business days; on request: within 3 business days; each provider or facility gives its own.

title: 45 CFR 164.524: Access of individuals to protected health information

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union

Art 9(1) health is special category; 9(2)(h) and 9(3) health care under professional secrecy; Art 12(3) one month, extendable by two months with notice in the first month; Art 28(3) processor contract; Art 33(1) 72 hours to the supervisory authority; Art 34 tell people when high risk; Art 35(3)(b) DPIA for large-scale special category data.

supports: Opened with WebFetch. Self-assessment against the National Data Guardian standards; all organisations with access to NHS patient data and systems must use it; 2026-27 version 9 outcomes, assertions and evidence items published 2 Oct 2026.

supports: Opened with WebFetch. Last updated 15 Oct 2026. Final report 24 Mar 2026; Order and RCVS undertakings published 22 Sep 2026; case closed 22 Sep 2026; first phase for larger businesses from 23 Dec 2026; smaller businesses get longer.

title: Small veterinary businesses: complying with the CMA's Order
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 13 Oct 2026, updated 15 Oct 2026. Businesses with 14 or fewer practices; price list (36 Schedule 1 services); written estimate at 500 pounds incl. title: Rest breaks at work
supports: Opened with WebFetch. One uninterrupted 20-minute break when working more than 6 hours; 11 hours rest between working days; 24 hours a week or 48 hours a fortnight; contracts may give more.

title: Overtime Pay
publisher: US Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Non-exempt employees get at least 1.5 times the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek; workweek is a fixed 168-hour period; no averaging across weeks; no extra federal pay for weekends as such. No page date.
